abstraction: etc/bridge/layout.h: bridge ABI byte facts (MESH_OFFSET_MESH_PAGE_ENTRY_ADDRESS, MESH_OFFSET_MESH_STREAM_READY, MESH_SIZEOF_MESH_DMA_SPAN, MESH_SIZEOF_MESH_BUFFER) in every planner consumer
handles: Sizing struct mesh_node_health's model field with MESH_MODEL_BYTES at line 389.
replacement: split the header: the planner's header names pages, nodes and steps only; the bridge's byte-offset ABI stays in the effector's headers
note: new group: a chooser header or file reaches pointer or byte-offset declarations for an unrelated constant; the one answer is header scope, not a page-map operation.

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: buffer 0 = the operand, the result made in place
handles: Lets a step read and land in the caller's operand without a copy between the send operand and the result.
replacement: lifetime allocation: the result's virtual pages share the operand's physical pages only where the solved lifetimes allow it; a step names a logical operand position and the page map, never buffer 0

function: struct mesh_step / struct mesh_move / struct mesh_program (buffer b >= 1, scratch)
violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: numbered scratch buffer b >= 1, a copy of the operand made at the call's start; mesh_program.scratch the most scratch buffers a rank uses
handles: Gives partial sums and forwarded pieces storage apart from the operand.
replacement: lifetime allocation of the program's intermediate values onto physical pages; the program names values and their lifetimes, not numbered buffers

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: a keep-alias or separate-source-generation flag per placed-page overwrite (preserve, separate[k])
handles: Breaks a cycle where an overwrite of placed pages must wait on a read of the same pages.
replacement: lifetime allocation over the composed invocation map: a read and an overwrite of one physical page are an interference edge, answered by assigning another physical page, not by a separate-generation flag

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: relay fragments in separate, compact, uninitialized leases as numbered buffers past initialized[r], each with a byte extent; offsets and buffer numbers differ at the two endpoints
handles: Gives a relay rank storage for fragments it forwards, apart from its logical buffers.
replacement: lifetime allocation of relay fragments' virtual pages; the extent is the image size of the solved map

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: distinct scratch per forwarded partial; a separate immutable source binding for the original contribution
handles: Keeps a contribution readable by its SEND while the result over the same operand can change.
replacement: lifetime allocation: the contribution and the result are two values; they share physical pages only where their lifetimes do not overlap

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: buffer 0 at q's segment for each SEND, buffer 1 at q's segment for each COPY
handles: Tells an all-to-all's send operand from its receive operand by fixed buffer numbers.
replacement: a step names the declared operand (source or destination) whose page map composed with its layout gives segment q's virtual pages

handles: Nothing this file uses: the solver calls none of the declarations mesh-call.h or mesh-dataflow.h bring in.
replacement: include mesh-plan.h and mesh-graph.h alone; region mapping and stream words stay in the effector's files
note: same group as mesh-plan.h:5: header scope gives the solver a pointer-yielding API it never needs.

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: buffer[u*n+v] = next++ from 2: a numbered scratch buffer per recipient whose heaviest tree has u inner; program scratch = the most a rank uses
handles: Gives each forwarded partial of a single-phase all-reduce storage apart from the operand and from other recipients' partials.
replacement: lifetime allocation of each partial value onto physical pages; the program names the partial (tree, recipient), not a buffer number

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: buffer[u*n+u] = 1, a separate immutable source generation, unless the operand is sent to one node only and u receives no result (then buffer 0)
handles: Keeps a rank's original contribution readable by its SENDs while buffer 0 already receives the reduced result.
replacement: lifetime allocation: the contribution and the result are two values whose lifetimes overlap, so they get different physical pages; no fixed generation number

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: receiver buffer 0 where w is the recipient (437); out = in = 0 for every move of the tree forms (470, 473): the operand made in place
handles: Lands each reduction and broadcast piece in the caller's operand so the result needs no copy.
replacement: lifetime allocation: the result's virtual pages map onto the operand's physical pages where the solved lifetimes allow; moves name values, not buffer 0

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: messages joined where last->out == m->out and last->in == m->in (hand-numbered buffers) and parts adjoin
handles: Joins adjoining parts sent between the same two nodes in one round into one message.
replacement: image: coalesce where the two parts' page images adjoin under the composed map, at both ends

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: definite initialization kept per numbered buffer b < scratch + 1; every buffer, scratch included, defined with the operand's range at the start
handles: Checks a program reads only defined values, taking every scratch buffer as a copy of the operand made at the call's start.
replacement: preimage: a read is defined where its virtual pages lie in the image of earlier writes under the composed map; no scratch is an operand copy

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: the required result checked in defined[0], buffer 0, the operand made in place
handles: Checks a required result is left defined, assuming it lies in buffer 0.
